description: Schema-neutral D06 research evidence. This file is not a parser, profile, or fixture contract.

stateVocabulary.documented: Affirmatively described by an official source for the named surface.
stateVocabulary.conditional: Settings-dependent, model-selected, experimental, or contradicted by another current official source.
stateVocabulary.not-listed: Absent from the current official support matrix for the named surface; not a permanent incompatibility claim.
stateVocabulary.unknown: Not defined precisely enough by the reviewed official sources.

scopeAssumptions.statement: GitHub's Copilot cloud agent support-matrix row maps to the hosted coding-agent surface represented by copilot-cloud-agent.
GitHub.com's code-review row maps to copilot-code-review; the separate local VS Code code-review row is outside this surface.
VS Code local Copilot Chat documentation maps to copilot-vscode; VS Code cloud-agent entrypoints map to the hosted coding-agent surface.
Documented syntax examples prove only the shown examples and are not treated as an exhaustive grammar.
A not-listed state is scoped to the retrieved support-matrix snapshot and does not claim permanent incompatibility.
Hosted observations require a timestamp because living service behavior may change without a client version.

facts.claim: Standard discovery locations include repository root, current working directory, intermediate directories, and directories nested in the path of a file being worked on.
.github/instructions/**/*.instructions.md is discovered recursively in standard locations except intermediate directories.
$HOME/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md and $HOME/.copilot/instructions/**/*.instructions.md are supported; COPILOT_HOME replaces that user root.
COPILOT_CUSTOM_INSTRUCTIONS_DIRS adds comma-separated directories for AGENTS.md and *.instructions.md discovery.
.github/copilot-instructions.md, path-specific instructions, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, and GEMINI.md are supported.
applyTo accepts comma-separated glob patterns and is evaluated against a file being worked on.
The pattern base for path-specific files found at nested discovery roots is not stated.
Relative @ references, including nested references, are expanded in copilot-instructions.md, AGENTS.md, and CLAUDE.md, but not GEMINI.md or *.instructions.md.
Repository references stay in the repository and local references stay in their custom-instruction directory; absolute and home-relative paths are rejected.
Cycle handling, maximum recursion depth, and symlink canonicalization are not documented.
Applicable user and repository files are combined and identical copies of selected user, repository-wide, and agent instruction files are removed.
General ordering, conflict winner semantics, and normalization used for deduplication are not documented.
Instruction changes require exiting and starting or resuming a CLI session before taking effect.
No hard size, count, import-depth, or aggregate-context limit is stated in the reviewed CLI page.
Discovery normally stays within open workspace roots; root .github/copilot-instructions.md is included for workspace chat requests.
.instructions.md files are discovered recursively below configured workspace and user instruction folders.
Trusted parent-repository customizations can be enabled when the workspace folder has no .git; the default setting is false.
Ordering and deduplication across multiple workspace roots are not documented.
applyTo is relative to the workspace root; comma-separated and brace patterns are shown, and ** matches all files.
The page both says missing applyTo prevents automatic inclusion and describes semantic matching via description, so description-only automatic activation is ambiguous.
Root AGENTS.md support is enabled by default with chat.useAgentsMdFile.
Nested AGENTS.md support is experimental, defaults false, and lets the agent select relevance based on edited files.
VS Code documents Claude-instruction support while GitHub's current VS Code Chat support-matrix row omits it.
Instruction files can contain Markdown links to files and URLs; referenced-instruction inclusion has a separate setting that defaults false.
Recursive loading, cycles, depth, containment, and equivalence to CLI @ references are not documented.
Multiple files can be combined and no specific order is guaranteed; personal instructions have higher priority than repository instructions, then organization instructions.
No local VS Code Chat effect for hosted-agent excludeAgent values is documented.
No hard instruction file size, count, link-depth, or aggregate-context limit is stated.
Repository-wide, path-specific, AGENTS.md, root CLAUDE.md, root GEMINI.md, and organization instructions are supported.
Path-specific instructions use comma-separated applyTo globs and combine with repository-wide instructions when matched.
The glob base and full dialect are not defined in the reviewed GitHub-hosted page.
One or more AGENTS.md files may be nested; the nearest one in the relevant directory tree takes precedence.
excludeAgent: cloud-agent excludes a path-specific file from coding-agent use; omission permits both hosted agents.
Repository instructions have higher priority than organization instructions, while all relevant instructions are passed.
No @ import, Markdown-import recursion, boundary, cycle, or depth behavior is documented for the hosted coding agent.
The reviewed sources do not pin the repository branch or lifecycle snapshot used for every coding-agent stage.
No hard per-file, aggregate, nesting, or import limit is stated.
Root copilot-instructions.md, path-specific instructions, root AGENTS.md, and organization instructions are supported for GitHub-hosted code review.
The review-specific page names root AGENTS.md while a generic GitHub-hosted page describes nested AGENTS.md, so nested review behavior is unresolved.
CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md are not listed in the current GitHub.com code-review support-matrix row.
Path-specific instructions apply to reviewed files matched by applyTo.
The glob base and formal dialect are not stated.
excludeAgent: code-review excludes a path-specific file; omission permits both hosted agents.
Code review reads instruction content from the pull request head branch.
Review can be manually requested; automatic review and re-review after pushes are separate configuration choices.
Code review does not follow external links in custom instructions.
Internal references, @ imports, recursion, cycles, containment, and maximum depth are not documented.
About 1,000 lines is advisory guidance intended to reduce ignored instructions, not a hard limit.
Ordering among repository-wide, path-specific, and agent instruction files is not stated.

crossSurfaceRules.claim: Syntax recognition is independent from surface activation; unknown activation is not invalid syntax.
There is no universal Copilot precedence or ordering model.
excludeAgent values affect only their named hosted surfaces.
Glob bases and dialect details are surface-specific; only VS Code explicitly states workspace-root relativity.
CLI @ reference behavior must not be projected onto VS Code or hosted surfaces.
Undocumented activation, ordering, reference, and limit behavior remains unknown.
The code-review 1,000-line statement is advisory and cannot cause a hard validation failure.
Branch provenance is surface-specific; code review documents head-branch loading while coding-agent lifecycle behavior remains unknown.
Client observations require pinned versions or hosted timestamps because the official pages are living documentation.

unresolved.summary: VS Code description-only activation is internally ambiguous in the current instructions page.
VS Code Claude support is documented by VS Code but omitted by GitHub's VS Code Chat matrix row.
Nested AGENTS.md support for hosted code review differs between generic and review-specific page scope.
CLI and hosted GitHub glob bases are not stated for nested path-specific files.
Within-repository instruction ordering is not defined across the four surfaces.
Reference and import behavior cannot be shared across CLI, VS Code, and hosted clients.
Symlink, canonicalization, case, deduplication-normalization, recursion, and hard-limit rules are incomplete.
VS Code multi-root workspace ordering is not documented.
